courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Families and Children
courses.description: This course will consider family from a life-course perspective and family influences on child development. Research and theory concerning divorced and step families, single parents, gay and lesbian parents, and family processes that shape children's development will be examined.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Psychology of Mental States and Language Use
courses.description: Examines how language use is affected by one's reasoning about the mental activities of others. We will examine the development of language, adult language use, and the language of autistic individuals, who are known to have difficulty reasoning about others' minds. This seminar will follow a discussion format. Honors version available.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Positive Psychology: The Science of Optimal Human Functioning
courses.description: This course invites students to explore the opportunities presented by the vibrant and emerging field of positive psychology.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Use, Misuse, and Addiction to Drugs in the 21st Century
courses.description: This is a first-year seminar on the use of drugs in the U.S. Its purpose is to understand the effects of drug use on pain management, overdose prevention, substance use disorder, overdoses, diversion, legal consequences, public health policy, harm reduction, and treatment. Activities include lectures from technical experts, post-lecture discussions, readings and student-lead discussions, written summaries of class material, formal debates, and a final class project on an effective evidence-based overdose prevention program.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Eating Disorders and Body Image
courses.description: Students will learn about anorexia and bulimia nervosa, as well as prevention and treatment efforts. The course explores factors related to these disorders and body image from a psychosocial perspective. Learning will occur through discussions, readings, videos, guest speakers, experimental assignments, writing assignments, and research projects.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Senses of Animals
courses.description: This course deals with the sensory systems of animals. A description of the human senses is included, but senses that differ from our own are emphasized. Some treatment of research methods is also included. Classes will be a mixture of lecture, discussion, and student reports.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Psychology of Emotion
courses.description: This first-year seminar is designed for students interested in exploring the psychological study of emotion. Topics include theoretical models of emotion process and structure, as well as a review of research questions about emotional expressions, autonomic physiology, affective neuroscience, emotion and reasoning, and emotion and health.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: First Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester. Honors version available.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology
courses.description: PSYC 101 is a prerequisite for all psychology courses. This course will give an overview of the many different scientific perspectives from which to understand behavior, including the biological, cognitive, developmental, social and psychopathological perspectives. This course is offered in two formats: a large-course format and as a First-Year Launch.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Reasoning with Data: Navigating a Quantitative World
courses.description: Students will use mathematical and statistical methods to address societal problems, make personal decisions, and reason critically about the world. Authentic contexts may include voting, health and risk, digital humanities, finance, and human behavior. This course does not count as credit towards the psychology or neuroscience majors.

source.text: PSYC 115. | 3 Credits. | FC-QUANT. | MATH 115 , BIOL 115 , STOR 115 .

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Media, Technology, and the Adolescent Brain
courses.description: In this course, we will learn about current evidence, theory, and controversies with regards to how technology use may affect adolescent development. Questions such as how technology is changing adolescents' social relationships, impacting their mental health, and interacting with the developing brain to influence social, emotional, and cognitive development will be explored.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Special Topics in Psychology
courses.description: An undergraduate seminar course that is designed to be a participatory intellectual adventure on an advanced, emergent, and stimulating topic within a selected discipline in psychology. This course does not count as credit towards the psychology major.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Statistical Principles of Psychological Research
courses.description: Consideration of the methodological principles underlying psychological research, descriptive and inferential techniques, and the manner by which they may be employed to design psychological experiments and analyze behavioral data. Three lecture hours. Students may not receive credit for both PSYC 210 / PSYC 210H and PSYC 215/PSYC 215H. Honors version available.

source.text: PSYC 210. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PSYC 101 or NSCI 175 . | FC-KNOWING or FC-QUANT.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Biopsychology
courses.description: Introductory course which surveys the biological bases of behavior. Topics may include nerve cells and nerve impulses, sensory systems, wakefulness and sleep, reproductive behaviors, and cognitive functions. This course would be an appropriate foundational course for Advanced Biopsychology (PSYC 402). Honors version available.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: Topics in attention; memory; visual, auditory, and other forms of information processing; decision making; and thinking. Honors version available.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
courses.description: Overview of clinical psychology: history, scientific basis, and major activities and concerns, including assessment, psychotherapy and other psychological interventions, community psychology, ethics, and professional practice. Honors version available.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychopathology
courses.description: Major forms of behavior disorders in children and adults, with an emphasis on description, causation, and treatment. Honors version available.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Child Development
courses.description: Study of the development of social and intellectual behavior in normal children and the processes that underlie this development. Emphasis is typically on theory and research. Honors version available.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: Introductory survey of experimental social psychology covering attitudes, interpersonal processes, and small groups. Honors version available.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Methods in Psychology
courses.description: Students in this course will be exposed to a survey of methodology (i.e., experimental, quasi-experimental, non-experimental) used across various disciplines in psychology (i.e., social, clinical, development, cognitive, and neuroscience). Class time will also be used to discuss methodological considerations in psychological research more broadly.

courses.title: Current Topics in Psychology
courses.description: Various special areas of psychological study, offered as needed. Course may be repeated for credit. Honors version available.

courses.title: Service Learning in Psychology: APPLES
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Service learning component for students enrolled in psychology APPLES courses. May not count toward the major.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Applied Statistical Methods in the Psychological Sciences
courses.description: This course extends statistical and data analytic concepts covered in PSYC 210 with direct applications to empirical data commonly encountered in psychological research. Topics include measurement, group comparisons, linear associations, and prediction. An equal balance is placed on statistical concepts, computer-based data analysis, and interpretation of findings.

courses.description: Recommended preparation, PSYC 210 or another quantitative reasoning course. An introduction to the interdisciplinary study of the mind, intelligent behavior, information processing, and communication in living organisms and computers.

courses.title: Pedagogy Course for Psychology & Neuroscience Undergraduate Learning Assistants
courses.description: This course gives an overview of teaching methods that facilitate the acquisition of knowledge and understanding as well as entails hands-on experience in the classroom. Common misconceptions of learning as well as legal and ethical considerations related to working closely with an undergraduate population will also be covered. Departmental application and approval required.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology and Neuroscience Undergraduate Learning Assistant
courses.description: This course is for students that have already served as a ULA and completed an associated pedagogy course. Students will gain additional hands-on experience supporting learning in the classroom and preparing supplemental learning materials. Departmental application and approval required.

courses.title: Clinical Psychopharmacology
courses.description: This course will investigate the pharmacological effects and the clinical efficacy of drugs used to treat behavior disorders.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Human Memory
courses.description: This course explores classic and current issues in the study of human memory. Topics include working memory, encoding and retrieval processes, implicit memory, reconstructive processes in memory, eyewitness memory, developmental changes in memory, neuropsychology and neuroscience of memory and memory disorders, memory improvement, and the repressed/recovered memory controversy.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Language
courses.description: Recommended preparation, PSYC 230 or LING 101 or LING 400. This course examines the mental representations and cognitive processes that underlie the human ability to use language. Covers what people know about language, how they process it, and how people make inferences about the speaker's meaning based on context. Recent work in experimental psycholinguistics is discussed.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Behavioral Decision Theory
courses.description: Simple mathematical and psychological models of judgment and choice, and related experiments, are treated, as are applications to real world problems in medical, environmental, policy, business, and related domains.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Gender and Pronouns
courses.description: This course offers an inside look at pronouns from an interdisciplinary perspective. From a cognitive perspective, we examine major models of the role that pronouns play, and the mental processes involved in using them. From a social perspective, we examine the role pronouns play in marking gender identity, and how both language usage and gender concepts are currently in flux. Students also learn about research methods and conduct a novel empirical study.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Topics in the Psychology of Language
courses.description: Examines the cognitive mechanisms behind language comprehension, focusing on how we make predictions about the speaker's meaning, based on context, background, gestures, and other cues. In this course-based undergraduate research experience (CURE), groups of students generate novel research questions, perform their own research experiments, and present the results in spoken and written format.

courses.title: The Development of Black Children
courses.description: PSYC 210 or 215 recommended. A survey of the literature on the development of black children. Topics include peer and social relations, self-esteem, identity development, cognitive development, school achievement, parenting, family management, and neighborhood influences.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Family as a Context for Development
courses.description: Explores how the family influences children's development. Topics include family theories, genetics, family structure (e.g., single parents, working mothers, divorce), discipline, parent behavior and values and beliefs, fathers and ethnic diversity.

courses.title: Evolution and Development of Biobehavioral Systems
courses.description: Examines the evolution and development of behavior patterns and their physiological substrates.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: The Study of Adolescent Issues and Development
courses.description: The developmental period of adolescence is studied from a multidisciplinary perspective. The course will distinguish among early, middle, and late adolescence and will cover several theoretical perspectives.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Development
courses.description: This course examines social influences on child and adolescent development, with a focus on advanced research methods in social-developmental psychological science. Topics include socializing agents of development (e.g., parents, peers, media), relationships and identity development, and the influence of social processes in developmental outcomes (e.g., academic outcomes, sexual behavior, mental health).
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, PSYC 101, and PSYC 210 or PSYC 270.

source.text: PSYC 473. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, PSYC 101 , and PSYC 210 or PSYC 270 .

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Digital Mental Health
courses.description: This course will provide an overview of the use of digital technologies to increase opportunities for training in, access to, and use of evidence-based mental health services. Coverage will include the current status of and future directions in research, innovations in service delivery, and policy implications. Special attention will be given to the evolution of the field, the potential costs and benefits, and the promise to address health disparities in particular.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Society and the Developing Brain
courses.description: Students will develop an integrated understanding of the cognitive neuroscience of brain development and the context of development. This course will provide an overview of principles of developmental cognitive neuroscience and will examine how societal structures shape the intimate environments of the family, school systems, and community contexts.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research in Digital Technology and the Developing Mind
courses.description: Empirical examination of how digital technology use interacts with psychological development. Students will identify a research question of interest, design a study to address that question, obtain relevant data through publicly available sources or novel data collection, analyze those data, and disseminate findings in written, visual, and oral formats.

courses.title: Theoretical, Empirical Perspectives on Personality

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Adulthood and Aging
courses.description: A developmental approach to the study of adulthood, from young adulthood through death. Topics include adult issues in personality, family dynamics, work, leisure and retirement, biological and intellectual aspects of aging, dying, and bereavement.

courses.title: African American Psychology

courses.title: Health Psychology

courses.title: Psychotherapy: Practice and Research
courses.description: This is a course on the treatment of psychological problems through the application of interventions grounded in psychological theory and focusing on behavior or mental processes. Students will become familiar with the more popular schools of psychotherapy, including their historical context, techniques, theoretical underpinnings, and research support. Honors version available.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Popularity, Friendship, and Peer Relations
courses.description: This course will review literature regarding peer relations among children and adolescents, including peer acceptance/rejection, popularity, bases of friendship selection, peer crowds, romantic relationships, and theories of peer influence.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Mania and Depression
courses.description: The social, developmental, and biological contributions to mania and depression are examined, as well as the impact of these moods on the brain, creativity, relationships, quality of life, and health.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Addiction
courses.description: PSYC 270 (Research Methods) and 245 (Abnormal Psychology) are encouraged but not required. This is an advanced seminar for undergraduate students that provides a comprehensive overview of the scientific study of addiction. This course will focus on the etiology and treatment of addiction to mood altering substances such as alcohol and illicit drugs, although many of the principles reviewed are applicable to behavioral addictions (e.g., gambling). Honors version available.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Creating Digital Tools for Positive Youth Development
courses.description: In this upper-level course, students will learn about the interdisciplinary field of Positive Youth Development and create a digital tool to improve health, well-being, or developmental outcomes for youth through an intensive semester-long project.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychological Archival Data Science
courses.description: This course addresses techniques in answering new questions with existing data. Students will learn about data from multiple perspectives: different data source and types, intended audiences, and visualization, analysis, and presentation formats. This will make students more savvy consumers as well as producers of data.

courses.title: Clinical Research: Design, Analyze, Disseminate

courses.title: The General Linear Model in Psychology
courses.description: Consideration of multiple regression and the general linear model in psychological research, including hypothesis testing, model formulation, and the analysis of observational and experimental data. Honors version available.

Project development and data collection will be in Python, and we will briefly explore R to analyze and visualize our results. No background in coding is required to take this course.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Statistical Illusions: Becoming a Critical Consumer of Research
courses.description: Information abounds, and it can be hard to decipher when to trust a reported analytic result and when to be skeptical. Building from students' prior knowledge of statistical inference and research design, this course provides practice and guidance on critical thinking when reading or viewing data analytic results in psychology and neuroscience. The primary goal of this course is to provide students with data analytic literacy that can be used in academic and real-world settings (e.g., evaluating AI generated responses; news reports; influencers).

courses.title: Statistical Models in Psychology: Theory and Application I
courses.description: This course is designed for advanced undergraduate students and entering graduate students and provides an exploration of the theory and principles underlying the application of statistical models in psychological research. courses.title: Applied Machine Learning in Psychology
courses.description: As opposed to hypothesis-driven data analysis, machine learning takes an exploratory and predictive approach to data analysis. This course introduces machine learning approaches in psychology to identify important variables for prediction and uncover complex patterns in datasets, such as nonlinearity, interactions, or clusters. Classes include theoretical lectures and hands-on examples.

courses.title: Psychology of Race and Racism
courses.description: This course offers an overview of research investigating the psychological underpinnings and impacts of racialization, racism, and racial inequality. It will center research in social psychology, but will also feature work from other areas of psychology (e.g., developmental), as well as other social science disciplines (e.g., sociology, political science).

courses.title: Interpersonal Relationships
courses.description: This advanced course will comprehensively cover the social psychological literature on normally-developing interpersonal relationships, with implications for relationships with family, friends, co-workers, and romantic partners. courses.title: Stereotyping, Prejudice, and Discrimination
courses.description: PSYC 270 recommended. Examines the determinants, functions, processes, and consequences of stereotyping, prejudice, and discrimination. Prospects for change are considered. Class presentations and participation required.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Attitude Change
courses.description: A detailed consideration of the theoretical issues in attitude and belief change.

source.text: PSYC 566. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, PSYC 101 , 260 , and either 210 or 215.

courses.title: Practical Wisdom from Advanced Social Psychology
courses.description: Surveys cutting-edge research across the field of social psychology and how it matters for everyday life. Topics include morality, mind perception, judgment and decision making, happiness, affective forecasting, emotion, relationships, negotiation, personality, free will, stress/health, and religion. Clear communication of research also emphasized through figures, presentations, and papers.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: The Social Psychology of Self-Regulation
courses.description: PSYC 270 recommended. An intensive review of self-regulation theory and research, focusing on the cognitive, motivational, and affective processes involved in goal commitment, monitoring, and overriding behavioral responses.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Neuroscience
courses.description: Social neuroscience is the study of how social processes and experiences are represented in and influence the structure and function of the brain. This course will focus primarily on functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies of humans, though we will also discuss other brain imaging techniques and patient studies. Previously offered as NSCI 571.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Theoretical and Empirical Perspectives on Sex and Gender Differences
courses.description: An in-depth examination of psychological research and theory pertaining to the influence of gender on the lives of men and women. In general, emphasis will be placed on understanding gender as a social psychological construct.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Women and Gender
courses.description: This course will discuss theories, methods, and empirical research findings on the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social aspects of the psychology of women, as well as topics such as feminist psychology, intersectionality, bias in psychological research, sexual orientation, sexuality, lifespan development, work, and health. Men and masculinity, the psychology of transgender persons, and a critique of the gender binary are also discussed.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Science of Moral Understanding
courses.description: Each of us is committed to our moral values and often struggle to understand those who with different beliefs. This course will focus on difficult moral disagreements (e.g., abortion, euthanasia), using social psychology and related disciplines to reveal the basis of our moral judgments, the drivers of moral divides, and how best to bridge them. We will cover both theory and application, and practice having constructive dialogue and civil disagreement to forge moral understanding.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Positive Psychology
courses.description: This course examines positive psychology, also called the science of thriving. One basic premise of positive psychology is that thriving individuals and thriving communities require the presence and interplay of positive emotions, positive relationships, and positive meaning. A second basic premise is that thriving does not result simply by curing pathology and eliminating problems. Rather, thriving requires building and capitalizing on human strengths and capacities. Students will apply course concepts in their everyday lives.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Music
courses.description: Music has the ability to influence our emotions, spark creativity, and influence relationships. But what makes music so universal? We will cover topics such as how music makes us happy vs. sad, can music be used for therapy, and does music help with memory through the lens of psychological science.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology and Law
courses.description: Examines the legal system from the perspective of psychology methods and research, with a focus on criminal law. Discusses dilemmas within the law and between the legal system and psychology.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Evolutionary Psychology
courses.description: Major topics of general psychology are examined from an evolutionary perspective with an emphasis on empirical studies asking why much current human behavior and experience would have been adaptive for our early ancestors.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Brain & Behavior I
courses.description: Graduate standing required. A survey of psychological and biological approaches to the study of sensory and perceptual information processing, with an emphasis on touch and pain.

courses.title: Brain & Behavior II
courses.description: A survey of psychological and biological approaches to the study of basic learning and higher integrative processing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Advanced Biological Psychology: Central Nervous System
courses.description: Each fall one special topic will be covered in depth (e.g., neural bases of memory storage, homeostasis, and perception). Format includes lectures and seminar meetings with student presentations.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Applications of Experimental Psychology to Health Research
courses.description: This course provides a critical analysis of interdisciplinary research within experimental psychology, including such topics as psychopharmacology, psychoneuroimmunology, psychophysiology, and animal models of brain/behavior disorders.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Behavioral Pharmacology
courses.description: Basic principles of pharmacology and behavior analysis are considered in relation to drugs that affect the central nervous system.

courses.title: Clinical Psychopharmacology
courses.description: Examinations of the clinical efficacy, side effects, and neuropharmacological actions of drugs used in the treatment of behavioral disorders. Additional topics include the behavioral and neuropharmacological actions of drugs of abuse.

courses.title: Research Design and Statistics in Neuroscience
courses.description: Limited to graduate students in psychology, neuroscience, and neurobiology. Experimental design, hypothesis testing, power analyses, ANOVAs, regression, correlations. Hands on data analysis with you being able to use your own data sets. Analyses will be conducted with SPSS and Prism. Permission of the instructor.

courses.description: An in-depth treatment of research topics in behavioral and biological aspects of health psychology.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Neurons to Neighborhoods: Contributions to Neurobiological Development and Behavioral Consequences
courses.description: This course provides an overview of what the field of human neuroscience has revealed about neural structure and function with an eye to examining individual differences. Current knowledge about the neural mechanisms supporting cognitive and emotional function will be investigated in depth through chapters, review articles, and empirical studies.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: This course will highlight recent research regarding the cognitive and neural architecture of human memory or attention, with the emphasis placed on studies using cognitive neuroscience methods (e.g. fMRI, EPRs).

courses.title: Seminar in Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Discussion and critical evaluation of various theories of thinking; theories of concept formation, problem solving, and reasoning.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Professional Development for Careers in Research
courses.description: Graduate standing required. This course covers research strategies, research collaboration, giving talks, writing review papers, writing research reports, the peer-review editorial process, the grant-proposal process, the academic job search process, and nonacademic career.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Attention
courses.description: Graduate standing in psychology required. This course will introduce the major issues in attention research and highlight recent work examining the neural mechanisms of attention and its interactions with other cognitive and social-cognitive processes.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognitive Aging
courses.description: This course examines theories of human cognitive aging and how these theories seek to explain age-group differences in various domains of cognitive functioning (e.g., episodic memory, language, judgment).

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psycholinguistics
courses.description: Graduate standing in psychology required. This seminar addresses the mental processes underlying human's ability to use language at a number of levels. Specific topics vary.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Seminar in Cognitive Psychology - Human Memory
courses.description: Selective overview of topics in the study of human memory. Course will examine the findings from laboratory research to gain a better understanding of memory structure and organization.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Seminar in Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: Graduate standing in psychology required. Students conduct a supervised research project in cognitive psychology, and participate in discussion of current research and related ethical and methodological issues.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Advanced Cognitive Development
courses.description: This course covers the development of attention, perception, learning, memory, thinking, and language, beginning in infancy and covering the life-span from both information processing and Baldwin-Piaget approaches.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Advanced Social Development
courses.description: Current thinking and research relevant to social, emotional, and personality development across the life span. Topics include parent-child interaction, peer relations, aggression, competence, sex roles, and gender differences.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Developmental Psychology: Methodology I
courses.description: Philosophical and sociological perspectives on research in developmental psychology, with specific applications to ongoing projects. As announced.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Ethics and Professional Issues in Developmental Psychology
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide an introductory knowledge base of ethical and professional issues that guide the field of Psychology, with specific focus on the field of Developmental Psychology.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Developmental Psychobiology
courses.description: Provides an introduction to psychobiological research, focusing on early development in animals. Topics include embryology, developmental neurobiology, the development of sensory and communication systems, and social behavior. As announced.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Advanced Family Theory and Research
courses.description: Research related to family processes, especially regarding the developmental consequences of varying family environments on children. Topics include divorce, cognitive development, single parents, parental employment, discipline, cultural context.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Seminar in Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Intensive study of selected topics in developmental psychology.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Development of the Social Brain
courses.description: The goal of this course is to understand the neural systems that support development from childhood to adulthood by drawing on theories and methods from developmental and social psychology as well as cognitive neuroscience. We will draw upon research examining the brain bases underlying the development of various social behaviors including social relationships, social stress, antisocial behavior, self-perception, and social influence.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Developmental Psychology Forum
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Presentations of research by faculty, students, and visitors; discussion of professional topics.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Proseminar in Developmental Science
courses.description: Intensive study of selected topics in human development that are being explored by members of the Carolina Consortium on Human Development staff. Permission of the instructor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: History of Psychology
courses.description: Review of the history of major areas of psychology, with special emphasis on the conceptual and methodological underpinnings of the discipline.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Special Readings in Psychology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Intended for advanced graduate students.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Professional Problems in Psychology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Consideration of problems facing academic psychologists.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Laboratory in College Teaching
courses.description: Specific training in presentational and interpersonal skills needed by college teachers, such as planning, lecturing, discussing, motivating, and evaluating.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive and rigorous introduction to the technique of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Students will learn the basic physics underlying MRI; the biological principles of fMRI, the principles of experimental design, data analysis, the use of available software packages, and special considerations for patient research.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Seminar in Biomedical Imaging Science
courses.description: This course serves as a gateway course to the Graduate Certificate in Biomedical Imaging Science. This course offers an introduction to the most common imaging modalities, including MR, CT, PET, SPECT, ultrasound, and optical imaging. Lectures include discussions of hardware, physics, as well as pre-clinical and clinical applications.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Advanced Clinical Science for Child and Adolescent Populations
courses.description: This graduate-level course is intended to strengthen and extend materials covered in the PSYC 809 : Introduction to Clinical Science course and is required of all clinical students in the child/family track. PSYC 803 sits at the intersection of theory, research, and practice and serves as an essential building block in an integrated sequence of coursework, research, and applied experiences that aim to empower clinical scientists to understand how behavioral and mental health problems develop and to apply an evidence-informed lens to improve well-being within and across systems through prevention and intervention.

Students will critically evaluate diagnostic models, transdiagnostic approaches, and cultural influences on psychopathology while developing case conceptualization and treatment planning skills.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Clinical Research Methods
courses.description: Graduate status in clinical psychology required. Analysis of clinical and personality research in terms of their contribution to knowledge, their limitations, possibilities for their improvement, further research they suggest, etc. Preparation of individual research proposals for class presentation and critical evaluation. Three hours a week.

courses.title: Advanced Research Methods for Clinical Science
courses.description: This is a graduate course for adult- and child/family-track students in the UNC-CH clinical psychology doctoral program and is intended to strengthen and extend material covered in the prerequisite: PSYC 762 Foundational Methods of Psychological Science or PSYC 806 : Clinical Research Methods. The course complements the broader training objectives of the UNC-CH clinical psychology doctoral program, emphasizing advanced elements of design that impact testing of the etiology, maintenance, and treatment of psychopathology across the lifespan.

Students will learn to approach the research, assessment, and treatment of these problems as clinical scientists.

Two lecture and two laboratory hours a week.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Assessment Across the Lifespan
courses.description: Theory, research, and application of objective and projective techniques for behavioral, emotional, psychiatric, interpersonal, and social cognitive assessment of cases across the lifespan (e.g., child, adolescent, adult). Two lecture and two laboratory hours a week.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Ethics and Clinical Interviewing
courses.description: This is a foundational course required of all first-year clinical students. The course includes an overview of ethics, ethical decision-making, and intake interview skills. Since students typically have had training in research (e.g., CITI Program's Responsible Conduct of Research, Good Clinical Practice), this course will focus more explicitly on ethics related to clinical practice. As such, this course lays the groundwork for subsequent clinical courses and practicum.

courses.title: Advanced Adult Practicum and Professional Ethics
courses.description: Supervised clinical work in an area of particular interest to the student. Clinical activity is coordinated with reading and discussion of literature or professional ethics.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Foundations of Clinical Neuroscience
courses.description: This course will survey contemporary neuroscience approaches to understanding mental illness, including mood, anxiety, and personality disorders, as well as addiction. We will also discuss the role of neurodevelopment and stress in the etiology of psychopathology. Students will become familiar with empirical studies encompassing animal models, computational models, and systems and molecular neuroscience. Finally, we will consider the tensions and synergies between psychological and neurobiological approaches to mental illness.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Integrative Topics in Clinical Science
courses.description: Required by accreditation standards for doctoral training in clinical psychology, this course addresses topics in supervision and consultation within clinical science and facilitates the integration of broad domains of discipline-specific knowledge within non-clinical areas of psychology as guided by the interests of each student.

courses.title: Seminar in Clinical Psychology

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Clinical Supervision and Consultation: Theory, Research, and Practice
courses.description: This course will familiarize fourth year clinical psychology doctoral students with methods and models of clinical supervision and consultation in an ethical and multicultural context. Includes a didactic seminar component and an applied supervision training component. Restricted to fourth year doctoral students in clinical psychology.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 1 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Practicum
courses.description: Individualized clinical practicum for advanced doctoral students in clinical psychology, namely: supervised experience in psychotherapy, psychological assessment, and consultation. Practicum experience is paired with a seminar within the academic program of the clinical psychology doctoral program to discuss external community practicum experiences and relate these to academic coursework and earlier clinical training.

courses.title: Multiculturalism in Clinical Science
courses.description: Required by accreditation standards for doctoral training in clinical psychology, this course adopts a widely cited and empirically supported multicultural counseling framework to address group differences or diversity in clinical science. Using a cultural humility stance, students will expand their (1) awareness of their own assumptions, values, and biases regarding diversity; (2) knowledge about the worldview of clients from a diversity of backgrounds; and (3) competence in using therapeutic skills that address client diversity.

This data enables the possibility for intra-individual variability analysis (IVA), or how to quantitatively describe individuals' dynamic process.

courses.description: The goal of the course is to provide a firm foundation in the regression analysis of binary, ordinal, nominal, or count dependent variables. Students should have a solid background in OLS regression analysis and some familiarity with matrix notation.

courses.title: Quantitative Research Methods

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Psychobiology
courses.description: Psychological processes are increasingly being appreciated as key predictors of morbidity, mortality, and well-being. But how, exactly, do factors in the social environment "get under the skin" to influence health? This is the main question we will investigate in this course. We will accomplish this primarily through extensive reading and discussion of journal articles and presentations on a variety of biomarkers, physiological processes, and pharmacological approaches.

Students produce a term project applying IRT to assessment data, and / or addressing mathematical or computational aspects of IRT.
